I was diagnosed with Chronic Trapezius Tension at 33. I'm 45 now. Turns out I never had a trapezius problem at all. My muscles were tight because something else was making them tight — and no one in twelve years of physical therapy, massage, or ergonomic consultation ever screened me for what was actually firing them.
For twelve years, I "managed" a condition I didn't actually have.

Twelve years of weekly deep-tissue massage. Same therapist. Rachel. She has known the exact knot in my right trap by name for over a decade. She calls it "the boulder." She has spent probably 500 hours of her life

I had the proof on her phone. I had the text already written. “I know about him. I want you out by Friday.”

My thumb was on send when her phone buzzed with a voicemail.

I’m glad I listened to it first. Because what was on that voicemail is the reason I’m still married. And I think there’s a man reading this right now who’s about to make the same mistake I almost made.

My name is Greg. I’m 58. I own a body shop. I’ve been married to Dana for 31 years.

I’m going to tell you something men don’t say out loud.
